steps.body: Tangent's period is **π** (recall), so its general solution needs only **one family with a π step**: tan x = 1 gives x = π/4 + **πk** — no twin required, because the twin (5π/4) is just the k = 1 rung. A denser ladder from a shorter period.

predict.prompt: Sine's solution ladder needs TWO families (+360°k each). How many does tangent need?

options.label: One — tangent repeats every 180°, so a single ladder catches everything
Two, like sine — all trig functions pair up
None — tangent equations have single answers

predict.reveal: One ladder with a 180° step. Tangent's whole pattern lives in one branch and repeats every half-turn — drag one full copy and read its length — so θ + 180°k sweeps up every solution. That's why sine's two families MERGE for tangent.

widget.prompt: Trace y = tan x through exactly one copy of its pattern and stop where it first repeats — the ladder's rung spacing.
widget.successFeedback: One copy per 180° — the π in x = π/4 + πk. Climbing the ladder with k = 2 lands at π/4 + 2π ≈ 7.07, the entry above: every rung is one half-turn because that is how often tangent hands back the same value.
widget.lowFeedback: Still inside the first branch — the pattern hasn't restarted. Drag on until the new branch mimics the old one exactly.
widget.highFeedback: You've overshot into the second copy — back up to the first angle where the pattern restarts.

explanationVariants: One solution per π; [0, 4π) spans 4 π-lengths: 4 solutions (π/4, 5π/4, 9π/4, 13π/4).
The πk ladder places rungs every half-turn: four rungs fit in two full turns.

widget.prompt: How many solutions does tan x = 1 have on [0, 4π)?

commonErrors.feedback: 2 per 2π is sine/cosine counting. Tangent solves once per π: 4 in [0, 4π).
8 would need period π/2. Tangent's rungs are π apart: 4.

steps.body: Sine and cosine families can ALSO merge when the twins are exactly π apart. cos x = 0 has base solutions π/2 and 3π/2 — a π gap — so the two 2πk families collapse into the single dense family **x = π/2 + πk**. Always check the twin gap before writing two ladders.

explanationVariants: sin x = 0: twins 0 and π are π apart → one family x = πk (equivalently 0 + πk).
0, π, 2π, 3π, … march by π: a single merged ladder.

widget.prompt: The general solution of sin x = 0 is best written as:

options.label: x = πk (one merged family)
options.feedback: Right — the base solutions 0 and π sit exactly π apart, so their ladders interleave into one.

options.label: x = 2πk only
options.feedback: That misses π, 3π, 5π, … (sin π = 0 too). The merged step is π, not 2π.

options.label: x = π/2 + πk
options.feedback: Those are the solutions of COS x = 0 (where sine is ±1). Sine's zeros sit at the multiples of π.

explanationVariants: sin x = 1/2: twins π/6 and 5π/6 differ by 2π/3 ≠ π — the families stay separate; a πk step from π/6 would hit 7π/6 where sin = −1/2.
Merging is legal only for an exact π gap; 2π/3 isn't it.

widget.prompt: Can the two families of sin x = 1/2 (π/6 + 2πk and 5π/6 + 2πk) merge into π/6 + πk?

options.label: No — π/6 + π = 7π/6 has sine −1/2, not 1/2
options.feedback: Right — the twin gap is 2π/3, not π, so a π step leaves the solution set.

options.label: Yes — all trig families can use πk
options.feedback: Test one rung: sin(π/6 + π) = −1/2 ✗. Only exact-π twin gaps merge (like cos x = 0).

options.label: Yes, but only for negative k
options.feedback: The sign of k doesn't matter — π/6 − π = −5π/6 also has sine −1/2 ✗.

explanationVariants: tan x = −1: base solution arctan(−1) = −π/4, family −π/4 + πk. In [0, 2π): k = 1 → 3π/4 and k = 2 → 7π/4. Sum: 3π/4 + 7π/4 = 10π/4 = 5π/2 ≈ 7.85.
Tangent is −1 in Quadrants II and IV: 3π/4 and 7π/4, one π apart as the ladder demands.
hints: k = 1 and k = 2: the rungs 3π/4 and 7π/4. Sum them.

widget.prompt: Sum the solutions of tan x = −1 on [0, 2π), to hundredths.

commonErrors.feedback: 3.93 ≈ 5π/4 has tan = +1. The −1 rungs are 3π/4 and 7π/4; their sum ≈ 7.85.
2.36 ≈ 3π/4 is one rung only. Add 7π/4 ≈ 5.50: total 5π/2 ≈ 7.85.

steps.body: Match the step to the period.
takeaways: Sine/cosine twins merge into a π-step family only when exactly π apart (e.g. cos x = 0, sin x = 0).
Test a rung before trusting any merge.
steps.teaser: Next: transformed equations — the inside gets its own ladder first.

concept.body: Ladder steps: sin/cos use 2πk per twin (merge to πk only when twins sit exactly π apart); tan always uses πk on one seed.

explanationVariants: tan x = 0 at x = 0 (and every π): the family is πk.
Tangent's zeros are sine's zeros: the multiples of π.

widget.prompt: The general solution of tan x = 0 is:

options.label: x = πk
options.feedback: Right — one seed (0), tangent's π step.

options.label: x = 2πk
options.feedback: tan π = 0 too — the step is π, catching every multiple.

options.label: x = π/2 + πk
options.feedback: Those are tangent's WALLS (undefined), not zeros.
